newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end down, liquidation wipes out July.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end down, liquidation wipes out July.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower on Wednesday, led by July which fell sharply on continued long liquidation, pit sources said.

"We're still dealing with the liquidation in the July," said Mark Weidner, oilseeds analyst with Cargill Investor Services. "The commercials are on the short side of the market so we're lacking any underlying support.
"With the commercials holding the short side of the equation, the threat of delivery is there."
The July contract shed 21 cents a bushel and traded as low as $7.03-1/2, down nearly $1.00 from Monday's high.
Rumors have circulated for weeks that a commercial firm would deliver soybeans but none have been posted. CBOT said Wednesday there were 10,000 bushels registered for delivery.
Traders said the expanded margins imposed following Monday's limit declines prompted more long liquidation.

"With the expanded margins we have, there were some 'get me out' type of orders," a floor trader said. Longs "have taken a lot of heat out there the last few days and a lot of people just threw in the towel."
Soybeans ended down 21 to 1/2 cent per bushel with July off 21 at $7.11 and new crop November down four at $5.85-1/2.

New crop months ended a shade lower, insulated from the brunt of the selloff by perceptions the market was oversold. The November contract had dropped 58 cents a bushel in two days after the U.S. Agriculture Department's acreage forecast put plantings at a hefty 70.85 million acres.
Weather continued to weigh on new crop with forecasts showing nearly perfect growing weather for the weekend.
The July/November spread dropped 17 cents a bushel to close at $1.24-1/2, premium July. That was the narrowest closing spread since March 18 when it closed at $1.22.

Floor sources said the November contract was stuck in a tug-of-war between two funds on opposite sides. Traders said Griffin Trading sold at least 10 million bushels November while FIMAT Futures bought an estimated 11.5 million bushels. Merrill Lynch sold 3.5 million November and E.D. and F. Man International bought five million November.
R.J. O'Brien was said to be the largest seller in the July, accounting for at least four million bushels.

In options trade, Continental Grain sold 500 August $6.50 puts at 4-3/4 cents, CIS bought 500 November $7.50 calls at three cents, and Lind-Waldock sold 600 November $6.00 puts at 27-1/2 cents, floor sources said.
Options volume was estimated by CBOT at 40,000 contracts. Tuesday's volume of 60,112 contracts was a record.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 80,000 contracts, below Tuesday's actual volume of 97,133.
